comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax implementation status
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD is continuing discussions on profit allocation and global minimum tax (Pillar One and Two), with the EU having adopted the 15% minimum tax for member states and many other countries implementing laws with effective dates starting in 2024, though some jurisdictions where the company operates have not yet adopted corresponding legislation.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose compliance risks related to evolving global laws and international jurisdictional requirements, but they focus on distinct regulatory regimes: Intel highlights broad operational compliance (including IP, export controls, and privacy) with specific risks to new technology adoption (5G), whereas AMD focuses specifically on the implementation of the OECD's global minimum tax (Pillar Two). Both acknowledge the complexity and multi-jurisdictional nature of their compliance burdens, though AMD's disclosure is narrower in scope, targeting tax law changes rather than the broader operational and trade compliance landscape described by Intel.

sentences.text: We are subject to complex and evolving laws and regulations worldwide that differ among jurisdictions and affect our operations in areas including, but not limited to: IP ownership and infringement; tax; import and export requirements; anti-corruption; foreign exchange controls and cash repatriation restrictions; data privacy and localization requirements; competition; advertising; employment and labor; product regulations; environment, health, and safety requirements; and consumer laws.

For example, unfavorable developments with evolving laws and regulations worldwide related to 5G or autonomous driving technology and MaaS may limit global adoption, impede our strategy, or negatively impact our long-term expectations for our investments in these areas.

The OECD is continuing discussions surrounding fundamental changes in allocation of profits among tax jurisdictions in which companies do business, as well as the implementation of a global minimum tax (namely the "Pillar One" and "Pillar Two" proposals).

Although many countries have already introduced Pillar Two legislation applicable to us effective in 2024, certain jurisdictions in which we operate have not adopted corresponding legislation to date.

comparisons.peer_summary: Tax incentives are subject to compliance conditions; failure to comply could require refunding benefits or losing them early, and modifying operations or strategy may not yield equally beneficial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom discuss compliance obligations, but the nature of the risk differs: Intel emphasizes the risk of employee/agent violations and the failure of internal controls to assure compliance, leading to potential fines and sanctions. Broadcom focuses on the compliance conditions attached to specific tax incentives, noting that failure to meet these operating conditions could result in the refunding of previously realized benefits. Both disclosures highlight that failure to adhere to regulatory or contractual conditions carries significant financial and operational penalties.

sentences.text: Our policies, controls, and procedures designed to help provide for compliance with applicable laws cannot provide assurance that our employees, contractors, suppliers, or agents will not violate such laws or our policies.
Violations of these laws and regulations can result in fines; criminal sanctions against us, our officers, or our employees; prohibitions on the conduct of our business; and damage to our reputation.
Each tax incentive and tax holiday is subject to our compliance with various operating and other conditions.

If we cannot, or elect not to, comply with any such operating conditions specified, we could, in some instances, be required to refund previously realized material tax benefits, or if such tax incentive or tax holiday is terminated prior to its expiration absent a new incentive applying, we will lose the related tax benefits earlier than scheduled.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk of Further Export Control Changes on Competitive Position
comparisons.peer_summary: Nvidia's competitive position has been harmed and may be further harmed long-term if USG export controls change. Rising geopolitical tensions and AI's strategic importance may lead to wider restrictions, potentially excluding Nvidia from China and other impacted markets like the Middle East.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA identify export controls as a critical and evolving area of regulatory risk that impacts their business strategies and competitive positions. Intel broadly cites 'import and export requirements' as part of its complex global regulatory landscape, while NVIDIA provides specific detail on how changes in US government export controls regarding AI products to China and other markets directly harm its competitive position and financial results. Both companies face the risk of government investigations and penalties due to these intense regulatory scrutiny environments.

sentences.text: We are subject to complex and evolving laws and regulations worldwide that differ among jurisdictions and affect our operations in areas including, but not limited to: IP ownership and infringement; tax; import and export requirements; anti-corruption; foreign exchange controls and cash repatriation restrictions; data privacy and localization requirements; competition; advertising; employment and labor; product regulations; environment, health, and safety requirements; and consumer laws.
The technology industry is subject to intense media, political, and regulatory scrutiny, which can increase our exposure to government investigations, legal actions, and penalties.
Our competitive position has been harmed, and our competitive position and future results may be further harmed in the long term, if there are further changes in the USG's export controls.

Given the increasing strategic importance of AI and rising geopolitical tensions, the USG has changed and may again change the export control rules at any time and further subject a wider range of our products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively impacting our business and financial results.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm is involved in various legal proceedings where unfavorable resolutions could materially adversely affect its business, financial condition, or cash flows, although the company intends to vigorously defend itself.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm highlight the risks associated with legal proceedings and regulatory scrutiny. Intel notes that intense media, political, and regulatory scrutiny can increase exposure to government investigations and legal actions, resulting in fines and reputational damage. Similarly, Qualcomm states that while it vigorously defends itself in various legal proceedings, the unfavorable resolution of these matters could have a material adverse effect on its business and financial condition. Both disclosures reflect the operational and financial vulnerability inherent in their respective legal and regulatory landscapes.

sentences.text: Violations of these laws and regulations can result in fines; criminal sanctions against us, our officers, or our employees; prohibitions on the conduct of our business; and damage to our reputation.
The technology industry is subject to intense media, political, and regulatory scrutiny, which can increase our exposure to government investigations, legal actions, and penalties.

We are also involved in other legal proceedings, including those described in this Annual Report in "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 7. Commitments and Contingencies." Litigation is inherently uncertain, and, while we intend to continue to vigorously defend ourselves in such matters, the unfavorable resolution of one or more of these matters could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows.
